articles.headline: Infosys Cuts Forecast Amid North American AI Slowdown
articles.brief: Indian IT giant Infosys has lowered its financial forecast, citing a deepening slowdown in North America driven by shifting enterprise spending priorities toward artificial intelligence technologies.

articles.headline: Amazon Cloud Capacity Sold Out Through 2027
articles.brief: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy revealed that the company's cloud computing capacity is completely sold out through 2027, highlighting unprecedented global demand for digital and AI infrastructure.

articles.headline: Seven Killed in Terrorist Attack at Jordan Church
articles.brief: Authorities in Jordan reported that seven people were killed and dozens wounded when gunmen opened fire during a funeral service at a church in the southern city of Karak.

articles.headline: Russia and Ukraine Agree to Local Humanitarian Ceasefire
articles.brief: Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia, and the United States reached a deal for a local humanitarian ceasefire in the contested southern town of Oleshky, set to begin on October 27.

articles.headline: Shein Agrees to Pay $100 Million to Settle FTC Probe
articles.brief: Fast-fashion retail giant Shein has agreed to a $100 million settlement with the US Federal Trade Commission following an exclusive investigation into its trade and business practices.

articles.headline: Kenya Announces Second Ebola Death Amid Strict Containment
articles.brief: Health authorities in Kenya confirmed a second Ebola death, a close relative of the index patient, while remaining infected individuals continue receiving treatment in secure isolation facilities.

articles.headline: India A Batters Suffer Collapse Against New Zealand A
articles.brief: On a grass-covered pitch favoring seam movement, the India A cricket team was bowled out for 113 runs, recording five ducks in a disastrous batting performance against New Zealand A.

articles.headline: France to Deploy 70000 Police for Weekend Protests
articles.brief: The French government will mobilize 70,000 police officers across major cities as high school student demonstrations over learning conditions merge with broader cost-of-living nationwide protests.
